title: DG6 - Dynamics
claim: A derivation layer can occupy coherent, defective, or ruptured states, allowing the grammar to describe successful derivation and failure modes.
assumptions: A framework must be able to classify not only valid structure but also damaged or failed structure.
definitions: Coherent: dependencies are preserved and the layer operates lawfully.
Defective: the layer exists but fails to preserve or express dependencies fully.
Ruptured: the layer collapses or loses required dependency structure.
negative_guards: Do not treat every imperfect claim as fully collapsed.
Do not treat defective as verified.
kill_conditions: The state classes cannot classify real framework failures without ambiguity.
The coherent/defective/ruptured categories collapse into mere rhetoric.
